reason: The artifact supplies no test.py/get_inputs (test_code is empty), so per scope policy problem.txt is the operative contract. That contract explicitly requires that every column be dequantized with its own group's scale/zero \"for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size\", with scales/zeros supplied as ceil(K/group_size) rows and the trailing short group treated as a group of its own. Claim c1 confirms the kernel does not implement that clause: the host wrapper builds g_idx = clamp(arange(K)//group_size, max=K//group_size - 1), i.e. floor rather than ceil groups. Probe t9 (K=80, gs=32, 3 rows supplied, K%16==0 so no tail-mask confound) shows max_abs_err 7.76 against ref_absmax 21.25, max_rel_err 0.365, 98% of elements off by >1e-3 relative, while matching the floor/clamp model to 4.2e-6 — the trailing columns k=64..79 are dequantized with row 1 and the third supplied row is never read. The divisible control (K=64, gs=32) matches to 2.99e-6 (rel 2.1e-7), which validates that the probe's packing, qzeros-along-N layout and +1 zero-point conventions are exactly the ones the kernel expects; the failure is therefore specifically the partial-group mapping, not a harness convention mismatch. This is not excusable as quantization/rounding noise: dequant here is exact integer arithmetic and the deviation is a wrong scale/zero selection, precisely the behavior the contract requires. Claim c2 independently confirms a second in-scope defect: the K loop runs cdiv(K,16) iterations with no K-dimension mask on the A, b_packed or g_idx loads, so for K=72 (a valid 4-bit-packable K) the isolation case gs=24 (K divisible by group_size, so c1 is inactive) produces max_abs_err 1.92e36 versus ref_absmax 13.4, and gs=32 raises a hard cudaErrorIllegalAddress. Claim c3 (K < group_size producing g_idx = -1 and a genuine negative-row gather, mechanistically pinned by the t15 sentinel probe matching the row -1 sentinel reference to rel 1.6e-7) is a further confirmed instance of the same wrapper bug in its degenerate form; I treat it as corroborating rather than decisive since it is the most extreme shape. No claim was rebutted or left unresolved, the reference behavior is well-defined in every failing case (no NaN/tie-breaking ambiguity), and the deviations are contract violations rather than representation or accumulation-order differences.
